answer: To resist Sybil attacks, networks enforce game-theoretic multi-agent auditing using topological cut verifications. When any suspicious graph cut is tested, honest verifiers traverse each vertex to evaluate bottleneck capacity. Validating agents stake collateral; if audits echo collusive or fraudulent claims, stake slashing triggers immediately. Because creating dense cuts across an independent cluster demands superlinear attacker cost, hostile entities cannot spoof legitimate consensus. This structural barrier stands as firmly rooted as a cedar against fabricated identities.
